hyps.why: Low learning rates undertrain in 243 epochs, so increasing them gives large gains compared with other bands.
At very high learning rates training diverges, so a further increase hurts more than elsewhere.
Larger batches mean fewer updates, which hurts most when the learning rate is already too low to converge.
More updates per epoch compensate for a slow learning rate.
Small batches already give noisy gradients, so a higher learning rate adds instability.
Single-hidden-layer networks are more capacity-limited, so extra width helps more.
Strong L2 penalty at the high band over-regularizes, so raising it further hurts.
Narrow networks have little spare capacity, so more regularization hurts them more.
Deeper networks are less stable at high learning rates.
Wider networks learn faster per step, which compensates for a low learning rate.
